title: A registry of DISPATCH ADAPTERS -- how one intelligence is started as a worker, and how what it produced comes back
description:
The hexagonal half of ADR-017 decision 2: the dispatch port knows no runtime, and a runtime is an ADAPTER. Like a runtime surface, this is the only kind of document allowed to carry a product's name, it is published in an adapter beside the kit, and the port finds it by the CONTRACT it keeps rather than by any list of publishers -- so a new intelligence is a new row in a new adapter and the port is never edited (Cardinal II, VIII).

A row is a DECLARATION and executes nothing (Cardinal IV). `starts.argv` is DATA -- a fixed argv with declared placeholders, no shell, no branch, no condition -- of exactly the class an activation block already names: the interpreter runs it and holds no knowledge of the product, the declaration holds no behaviour. The placeholders and return channels a row may name are the ones the PORT provides; a row naming any other is refused rather than substituted with an empty string, because a worker started with a silently blank instruction is the most expensive silence there is.

Everything a row says about somebody else's software is a CLAIM and stays one until a run of that product has been observed doing it -- which is what `says` is for, and why an adapter shipped before it has been measured is honest rather than green.

id.description: The id a packet's `route` names. One id, one declaration: a route that resolved to two adapters would be a name that is not a name.

says.description: Which product this starts, what is claimed about how it behaves, and where that claim comes from. Testimony, labelled as testimony -- including, explicitly, whether it has ever been observed on this machine.

starts.description: How the worker is started. The argv is run with its working directory set to the isolated workspace the port made for this task, never at the host root: the workspace IS the isolation (ADR-017 decision 5).

argv.description: A fixed argv. A part may carry placeholders in braces; the port substitutes only those it provides and refuses any other by name.

stdin.description: What is written to the worker's standard input, with the same placeholders. Absent means nothing is written and the stream is closed -- never an empty line that a prompt-reading process would take as an answer.

options.description: Parts appended to the argv only when the route gives the value they name (`when`): how this product is told the model, effort, spend cap or turn cap a route row declares. A value the route does not give adds nothing; a value the product cannot be told has no option here, and the adapter says so.

returns.description: The ARTIFACTS this worker produces, and the channel each is read from. Results come back as artifacts (A2A, adopted whole), never as a status message doing an answer's job.

from.description: The channel, by the name the port provides for it. An unprovided channel is refused, so widening the set is the port providing another one -- never an enum edited here.

carries.description: ADR-022: the kit schema this artifact's text is a document of -- `dispatch-return` for the worker's structured return. The port parses and validates it on return; a declared carrier that is absent or invalid closes the task as failed, by name.

completed_on.description: What this product's worker does when it finished the work, so the port need never DECIDE what an exit code meant. Anything else ends the task `failed`, with the code recorded beside the state.

asks.description:
How this product's worker says it CANNOT PROCEED and is asking a question rather than guessing -- and which of its declared `returns` carries that question. Optional: an intelligence with no such ending declares nothing here and can never put a task in `input-required`, which is an honest absence rather than a capability quietly assumed.

The question is read from a DECLARED CHANNEL and never recognised in a worker's prose: a port that knew what a question looks like would hold a grammar for somebody else's output and would find questions in answers. `exit` may not be the same code as `completed_on.exit` -- one ending cannot mean two states -- and the artifacts named here must be ones this row declares in `returns`, so nothing is read from a channel nobody declared.

exit.description: The exit code this product's worker uses for 'I need input'. A CLAIM about somebody else's software like every other, and `says` is where it is labelled as one.

question.description: The name of the artifact, declared in `returns`, that the worker's question comes back in.

reentry.description: The name of the artifact, declared in `returns`, carrying whatever re-enters THIS worker -- a session name, a handle, a resume token. Optional: a product resumed by where its work stands rather than by a name for its turn declares none, and its `resumes.argv` then names no `{reentry}`. It may not be the same artifact as `question`: one text doing both jobs could only be separated by this port parsing it.

resumes.description:
How an operator's answer is carried back into the worker that asked -- the SAME worker, in the tree it was left standing in. Optional and independent of `asks`, deliberately: an adapter that declares a way to ask and none to be re-entered is a real situation, and the task it parks says so at the moment the question was read rather than looking like one nobody has answered yet. A resume act against such an adapter is refused BY NAME.

The shape is `starts`' shape because a resume IS a start of the same worker; what differs is the argv the product declares and the two values the port provides only here -- `{answer}`, the operator's own words, and `{reentry}`, whatever came back on the channel `asks.reentry` named.

argv.description: A fixed argv, run in the same isolated workspace the worker was started in. Same placeholder rule as `starts.argv`, and no shell, no branch, no condition (Cardinal IV).

stdin.description: What is written to the resumed worker's standard input, with the same placeholders. Absent means nothing is written and the stream is closed.

options.description: Parts appended to the argv only when the route gives the value they name (`when`): how this product is told the model, effort, spend cap or turn cap a route row declares. A value the route does not give adds nothing; a value the product cannot be told has no option here, and the adapter says so.

usage.description: What this product reports about a run's cost, read out of one of its declared artifacts into the run record under OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention attribute names (`gen_ai.*`). `fields` maps an attribute to a dotted key into the artifact's JSON (`.@keys` takes an object's first key); `jsonl` reads a JSON-lines artifact, taking the LAST line whose fields equal `where`. A product that reports nothing declares nothing, and the record says the usage was not reported. A claim until a run is observed.

provider.description: `gen_ai.provider.name`, in the semantic conventions' own vocabulary.
